name: PETRA BAKE&COFFEE（ペトラ ベイク&コーヒー） (Petra Bake & Coffee)

claims.text: Wheat, including spelt wheat (used in the carrot cake), is baked on-site alongside rice-flour items in a single small shop, so cross-contamination is likely; no dedicated gluten-free area is mentioned.
Animal-product-free baked goods are offered on the same counter as dairy/egg items; no separate vegan prep is documented, and the carrot cake contains walnuts.
The bakery explicitly offers animal-product-free (vegan) items and soy milk for lattes, so plant-based diners have real choices.
Some items are made with rice flour (米粉), such as the banana bread, giving non-strict diners lighter-wheat options.

name: レストラン自由軒 (Restaurant Jiyuken)

claims.text: A fried-food and roux-heavy kitchen (cutlets, croquettes, demi-glace stews) where wheat is pervasive; cross-contamination is effectively unavoidable.
The signature omurice is flavored with a soy-sauce-based broth, and standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
Dishes are built around meat, eggs and dairy (stews, omurice, croquettes); shared cookware makes vegan-safe preparation unlikely.

name: シンタテベイクストア (Shintate Bake Store)

claims.text: This is a flour-based bakery using home-milled organic wheat and whole wheat as its core ingredient; airborne flour and shared surfaces make it unsafe for celiacs.
Many items contain dairy and eggs (e.g. canelé, cherry pie); no separate vegan production is documented.
Ingredients emphasize pesticide-free organic wheat and natural yeast with a 'healthy and delicious' philosophy, so the bread is made from carefully chosen, transparent ingredients.
The cooking is traditional Japanese seafood cuisine relying on dashi and soy-sauce-based seasoning, which in Japan normally contains wheat; no gluten-free accommodation is documented.
The menu is built around fresh fish and seafood with dashi-based seasoning; no vegan or plant-only dishes are documented.

name: 旬彩和食 口福 (Shunsai Washoku Kofuku)

claims.text: Menu is built on soy sauce, sesame-miso sauce, dashi and tea-broth preparations; no gluten-free handling is documented, so cross-contamination from wheat-based seasonings should be assumed.
Signature hitsumabushi and seafood bowls are served with soy sauce and a sesame-miso sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat and no GF soy sauce is mentioned.
Kitchen centers on fish, shellfish and dashi; no separate vegan preparation is documented, so cross-contact with animal ingredients is essentially unavoidable.

name: そば やまの葉 (Soba Yamanoha)

claims.text: The kitchen handles wheat-containing soba (soto-nihachi, ~20% wheat) and wheat-dough oyaki alongside the 100% buckwheat juwari, so shared flour and boiling water make cross-contact very likely even for the juwari noodles.
Soba is served with a soy-sauce-based dipping broth (tsuyu); standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
Broths are dashi-based and the menu features fish (negitoro) and tempura; no separate vegan stock is documented.

A genuine juwari (100% buckwheat) soba is on the menu, milled from local Torigoe buckwheat, for those avoiding wheat in the noodle itself (though shared equipment and the soy-based tsuyu remain concerns).

The signature soba is '九割そば' (nine-tenths buckwheat), meaning it contains roughly 10% wheat flour as a binder — the noodles are not gluten-free, and a shared soba-boiling kitchen makes cross-contamination with wheat likely.
Dishes such as the oyakodon and soba tsuyu use a dashi/kaeshi base; traditional kaeshi is made with soy sauce and mirin, which normally contain wheat. No wheat-free seasoning is documented.
Broths are based on bonito (katsuo) and kombu fish/seaweed dashi, and signature dishes feature chicken, egg, and shrimp, so plant-based diners cannot avoid animal-derived stock.
House soba is nihachi (二八), made with 20% wheat flour, so the noodles themselves contain gluten and there is no gluten-free option.
Soba is served with a traditional dashi/tsuyu, which in soba shops is wheat-soy-sauce based; no gluten-free tsuyu is documented.
The set centers on fish-dashi broth and seafood (sashimi, herring), so vegan separation is not offered.
